args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was ~18% with healthy=false.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production history (v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 both healthy; v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc only exists in staging and was unhealthy).

The initial rollback attempt partially failed — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate ~0.2%.

Follow-up: investigate root cause of v2.3.1 health check failures before any redeploy; do not redeploy v2.3.1 without change-manager approval since it has never been healthy in production.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully despite the timeout — INC-0001 exists and is open, so I did not retry (which would have risked a duplicate page).

## Summary

**Rollback completed and service recovered.**

- **Initial state:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), `healthy=false` with an ~18% error rate.
- **Target selection:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release with a healthy production history (v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 healthy; v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and unhealthy).
- **Rollback issue:** The first rollback attempt partially failed — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on the failing v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout.
- **Final state:** All three regions on v2.3.0, `healthy=true`, error rate ~0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 opened as SEV2 for checkout-api, documenting the failure, the partial-rollback-and-retry, and the current recovered state.

**Recommended follow-ups (not actioned):** Root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before any redeploy. Note that redeploying v2.3.1 would require change-manager approval under policy, since it has never been healthy in production.
